## 1. Executive Result  

A **complete, self‑contained probability‑space formalism** for the standard bipartite Bell (CHSH) scenario is presented.  All relevant notions – hidden variable λ, settings x,y, outcomes A,B, joint/conditional distributions, **measurement‑independence (MI)**, **parameter‑independence (PI)**, **outcome‑independence (OI)**, **factorisability**, and **determinism** – are defined with precise symbols, domains and logical relations.  

The ledger distinguishes three *levels* of assumptions  

| Level | Content | Category (Mathematical / Operational / Physical) |
|-------|---------|---------------------------------------------------|
| **M‑1** | Existence of standard Borel probability spaces for λ, settings and outcomes; existence of regular conditional probabilities. | Mathematical |
| **O‑1** | Experimenter’s ability to choose settings according to prescribed distributions *independently* of any hidden variable (the *free‑choice* or *measurement‑independence* premise). | Operational |
| **P‑1** | No‑signalling at the observable level (marginals of A do not depend on y and vice‑versa). | Physical |
| **P‑2** | Locality / *factorisability* of the response functions given λ (PI + OI). | Physical |
| **P‑3** | Determinism (outcomes are functions of λ and the local setting). | Physical (optional – can be relaxed). |

All Bell‑type results that follow from the CHSH inequality are **derived** from the conjunction **M‑1 ∧ O‑1 ∧ P‑1 ∧ P‑2**.  Removing **O‑1** yields the *measurement‑dependence* (MD) family; removing **P‑2** yields the *no‑signalling* (NS) family; removing **P‑3** yields the stochastic‑local model.  

The table below (Section 3) records each assumption, its formal statement, and its classification.

## 2. Definitions & Notation  

| Symbol | Meaning | Domain / σ‑algebra | Remarks |
|--------|---------|--------------------|---------|
| \( \Lambda \) | Hidden‑variable space | Measurable space \((\Lambda,\mathcal F_\Lambda)\) (standard Borel) | May be discrete or continuous. |
| \( \lambda \in \Lambda \) | Specific hidden‑variable value | – | Random variable with distribution \(P_\Lambda\). |
| \( X \) | Alice’s measurement setting | Finite set \(\mathcal X =\{0,1\}\) (or any finite alphabet) with σ‑algebra \(\mathcal F_X =2^{\mathcal X}\). | Often denoted \(x\). |
| \( Y \) | Bob’s measurement setting | Finite set \(\mathcal Y =\{0,1\}\) with σ‑algebra \(\mathcal F_Y\). | Denoted \(y\). |
| \( A \) | Alice’s outcome | Finite set \(\mathcal A =\{-1,+1\}\) with σ‑algebra \(\mathcal F_A\). | Denoted \(a\). |
| \( B \) | Bob’s outcome | Finite set \(\mathcal B =\{-1,+1\}\) with σ‑algebra \(\mathcal F_B\). | Denoted \(b\). |
| \(P_{X,Y}\) | Distribution of the *chosen* settings | Probability mass function on \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\). | In the *free‑choice* case \(P_{X,Y}=P_X P_Y\). |
| \(P_\Lambda\) | Prior distribution of the hidden variable | Probability measure on \((\Lambda,\mathcal F_\Lambda)\). |
| \(P_{A,B|X,Y,\Lambda}\) | **Response function** (conditional outcome law) | For each \((x,y,\lambda)\) a probability distribution on \(\mathcal A\times\mathcal B\). |
| \(P_{A|X,\Lambda}\), \(P_{B|Y,\Lambda}\) | Local response marginals (used when factorisability holds). |
| \(P_{A,B|X,Y}\) | Observable joint outcome distribution (obtained by marginalising over λ). |
| \(E_{xy}\) | Correlator \(\displaystyle E_{xy}= \sum_{a,b} a b \, P_{A,B|X,Y}(a,b|x,y)\). |
| \(S\) | CHSH expression \(\displaystyle S = E_{00}+E_{01}+E_{10}-E_{11}\). |
| \(I(XY:\Lambda)\) | Mutual information between settings and hidden variable (quantifies measurement‑dependence). |
| \(\epsilon\) | Total‑variation distance \(\displaystyle \epsilon = \frac12\!\sum_{x,y,\lambda}\!|P_{\Lambda|X,Y}(\lambda|x,y)-P_\Lambda(\lambda)|\). |

All probabilities are **non‑negative** and **normalised** (see Section 5).
